# Results

## Future self continuity and wellness behaviours

## Future self continuity, self rated health, and wellness behaviours

The meta-analysis of the associations between future self continuity and poor
FSRH across 16 samples revealed a negative relationship between the two
variables. (see Table XX). Heterogeneity tests indicated no significant
variability between the studies $(Q(15) = 21.19, p = 0.131, I^2 = 0.00\%, \tau^2 = 0.00$.

For poor FSRH and wellness behaviours, a consistent negative relationship was
observed across the same 16 samples, with an overall small effect effect size.
Significant heterogeneity was observed $Q(15) = 26.50, p = 0.033, I^2 = 32.65\$, \tau^2 = 0.002$
suggesting that moderator analyses were warranted.

Moderator analyses for the possible impact of sample type could not be conducted
as there were fewer than 3 studies per subgroup for each of the analyses.
Meta-regression testing of the potential influence of participant age on the
effect between poor FSRH and wellness behaviours was non-significant
$\beta = -0.001 \; [-0.01, 0.01]$, $Q_\text{model}(1) = 0.06, p = 0.79$,
$Q_\text{residual}(14) = 26.26, p = 0.024$. In addition, the meta-regression
of the potential impact of participant gender was non-significant
$\beta = -0.12 \; [-0.34, 0.11]$, $Q_\text{model}(1) = 1.04, p = 0.308$,
$Q_\text{residual}(14) = 25.34, p = 0.031$.

Finally, the meta-analysis of the semi-partial correlations (adjusting
for poor FSRH) between future self continuity and wellness behaviours suggested
a small effect. Heterogeneity tests were non-significant
$Q(15) = 21.44, p = 0.12, I^2 = 15.46\%, \tau^2 = 0.0008$ indicating that
moderator analyses were not warranted.
